newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov Pataki creates 7 economic development zones.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov Pataki creates 7 economic development zones.

text.p: New York State Gov. George Pataki, concerned that defense cutbacks are hitting some communities hard, is creating seven economic development zones.
The new zones are designed to help the areas make the the transition from a military-based economy to a civilian one.

Separately, the governor said he rejected a bill to set up five more industrial development agencies, one for each of New York City's boroughs. Each of the new agencies would have been allocated part of the city's share of private activity bonds.
Pataki explained the proposal to create the new Industrial Development Agencies flew in the face of one of his Administration's top priorities, consolidating government.
Further, he said that giving the five new entities the ability to grant tax relief would have undermined the city's and state's ability to control their finances.

Most importantly, the governor added he rejected the measure because it could have triggered competition between the boroughs for projects, and force the mayor, who would have had veto power, to choose the winner.
"A bidding war for projects could escalate the size of the tax exemption packages to the detriment of the city's and state's budgets," the governor said, in his message disapproving the bill.
